capitals.name: Santa Maria do Algarve (Faro)
capitals.note: The page gives only the name 'Santa Maria do Algarve' and does not mention Faro; the identification with Faro is the researcher's.

keyframe_review.note: 2,252 km2 on the Faro coast of the Algarve. The infobox gives no area and the page names no boundary beyond 'southern Portugal', so only size and bbox were checked.

correction.cliopatria: Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve

keyframe_review.note: The same 2,252 km2 shape, but the taifa ends in 1051, not 1055: infobox 'Conquered by the Taifa of Seville: 1051'; 'It existed from 1018 to 1051'. The shape stands for 1046-1050.

ledger.note: 1018: the Harunid taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve appears. Infobox 'Established: 1018'; 'Sa'id: c. 1018–1041/2'; it was 'located in what is now southern Portugal' and followed the Taifa of Badajoz. The page gives no boundary.

region.cliopatria: Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve

ledger.note: 1051: Seville conquers Santa Maria do Algarve. Infobox 'Conquered by the Taifa of Seville: 1051'; 'To Seville: 1051–1091'.

region.cliopatria: Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve

ledger.note: 1051: the taifa ends under Muhammad al-Mu'tasim and its land passes to Seville; 'their descendants remained as Qadis of the city until its reconquest by Portugal in 1249'.

wars.name: Abbadid conquest of Santa Maria do Algarve

zones.cliopatria: Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve

wars.outcome: Seville conquered the taifa in 1051 and held it to 1091.
wars.note: The page names no battle; the Seville page lists Santa María de Algarve among Abbad II's conquests without a year.

certainty.note: The page names the capital and 'southern Portugal' only; the coast is firm, the inland frontier with Badajoz approximate.

sources.title: Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve
sources.note: Identity: established 1018, rulers, capital, conquered by Seville 1051.

sources.title: Taifa
sources.note: First-period list 'Santa Maria do Algarve: 1018–1051 (Harunid Dynasty); 1051–1091 (to Seville)'.

notes: (1) Cliopatria ends the taifa in 1055, the page in 1051; the Seville dossier carries the gain in 1051. (2) The first attempt to open the page by its accented title failed (url_not_found); 'Taifa_of_Santa_Maria_do_Algarve' opened. (3) Faro is not named on the page; the capital dot at Faro is the researcher's identification of Santa Maria. (4) The infobox gives no area; Cliopatria's shape was compared by size only. (5) Cliopatria's Taifa of Silves 1040-1055 (6,223 km2) adjoins to the west; the Silves page says nothing of a boundary.
